title: Implement real space convolutions in scarlet
description: Currently all convolutions in scarlet are done in k-space. In general this is faster than doing them in real space, especially for large blends, but back propagating the derivative in autograd is an expensive procedure. There is also a possibility that numerical artifacts exist in back propagation though the FFTs, since this is effectively a deconvolution, but this is not yet clear. We expect to save cpu cycles by implementing convolutions in real space as well as potential numerical stability.    There are two other side benefits to using real space convolutions:    1. We can potentially avoid using autograd, which has an overhead in terms of memory used and extra processing.    2. If we decide to run scarlet on an entire patch in the future then we'll be forced to implement a spatially varying PSF, which is possible with real space convolutions but not using a single PSF in k-space.

title: Provide Simple Per-CCD Fix to Amp-to-Amp Offset Issue
description: This ticket explores two simple empirical approaches towards fixing the known amp-to-amp offset issue in HSC CCDs. Multiple attempts to provide a meaningful hardware-related solution to the amp-offset issue have been explored, with work ongoing in this regard. In the meantime, we provide these simple per-CCD fixes as a proof of concept. Should more desirable corrections not be forthcoming, this work serves as a potential future fix which can be applied to future datasets.    Techniques explored are per-amp background subtraction and amp-edge pattern continuity corrections. Both methods have their merits, however, per-amp background subtractions remain vulnerable to stray light (ghosts, ghouls, etc) or strong flux gradients. Conversely, amp-edge pattern continuity corrections perform well across multiple scenarios, with most remaining weaknesses solveable in the short-term. Therefore, if subsequently required, we recommend amp-edge pattern continuity corrections for future use.    Attachments below contain both example notebooks, a brief PDF presentation, and all postage stamps used within the PDF.  Full processing outputs can be found at: https://github.com/leeskelvin/amp2amp

title: Write outlier rejection code for IOD
description: To reduce the number of mixed linkages that come out of [~<USER>'s implementation of HelioLinC, we need to add outlier rejection to the IOD code. Given a maximum allowable contamination percentage, this code should iterate through different combinations of observations and flag any observations sufficiently far away from the best-fit orbit. title: Latency characterization for the Summit EFD with M1M3 +M2 data streams
description: Report on the latency characterization work done during the week of Feb 26 to Mar 4 when we first had [real M1M3 + M2 data streams at the Summit| https://lsstc.slack.com/archives/CM65SGAJE/p1582738049002700].    The first good news is that the EFD runing on a single server with Kubes (k3s) was able to keep up with the M1M3 (50Hz) + M2 (20Hz) data streams.    We noticed however, the presence of """"latency spikes"""" of ~20s every few minutes and decided to find the root cause and improve that.    We deployed the kafka control center to help us to monitor Kafka and from that tool it became clear that there was a lag in the consumer group for the Kafka InfluxDB connector where we observed a repetition pattern of ~1000 messages falling behind (connector lag)  and then getting restored. 1000 messages at 50Hz correspond to the ~20s latency spikes we observe.    To reduce the connector lag we added more partitions to the M1M3 and M2 kafka topics which increased the connector throughput and alleviated the problem reducing significantly those latency spikes. From the Kafka Control Center at the Summit https://control-center-summit-efd.lsst.codes/ we are using 18 partitions for M1M3 and M2 topics now. This way we have messages being consumed in parallel and to increase the throughput when writing to InfluxDB we could also increase the number of connector tasks.  Currently, we are running only one connector task, but we plan on increasing that soon.    That already improved the latency removing the ~20s spikes. The latency is now dominated by the SAL Kafka producer which also shows those spike features of ~2s from time to time.    To further improve latency we can increase even more the number of partitions, increase the number of connector tasks, have multiple connectors for different subsystems if needed, perhaps reproduce in Kafka Connect what we do with the SAL Kafka producers, and if needed increase the size of the Kafka Connect cluster.

Objectives  The proposed functionality of the Qserv Replication System would allow an efficient mechanism for:  * exporting (ready to be ingested) data for external users, LSST sites, or Qserv instances of the same site  * backing up catalog data  * _in-place_ re-partitioning and re-ingesting catalogs if a change in the partitioning configuration was required    This functionality would be especially useful (or be the only option) if the original (source) of data used for ingesting a catalog is either not-available, or it's difficult to use for (re-)ingesting the catalog.    h1. Implementation details  Here is a summary of changes/additions to the existing code:  * extending system's Configuration service to allow specifying an internal (at workers) _export_ directory where the *{{CSV}}*/*{{TSV}}*-formatted dumps of the tables/chunks would be temporarily stored before returned them to clients/requestors  * adding the _export_ service to be run at each Replication System's worker  * adding the client API (library) for interactions with the workers _export_ services  * adding a binary applications build upon the API for retrieving the data from the _export_ services and writing them as local files  * extending the REST API of the *Master Replication Controller* for retrieving connection parameters of the above mentioned _export_ services needed to retrieve a content of a _regular_ table or a _chunk_ (or _chunks_) of a _partitioned_ table  * unit and/or integration tests where it may seem feasible

title: DBB Buffer Mngrs v1.1 Implementation
description: ﻿The project is nearing the time when it will want to automatically ingest raw images into a friendly-user Gen3 butler repository. The DBB Endpoint Buffer Manager should be modified to be capable of ingesting raw images into Gen2, Gen3, and Rucio. Raw images will continue to arrive on the DBB gateway node via both the DBB Handoff Buffer Manager as well as the rsync raw image transfer service. The ingests into Gen2, Gen3 and Rucio should be able to work with raw images from either service. This will deprecate the cron job running on the gateway node to ingest rsync'd data into gen2 repos. Ingests will be configurable to make softlinks instead of move file into place. During friendly-user time, Gen2 butler will still be the production mechanism to serve raw images. Problems with Rucio or Gen3 ingestion should not cause delays or problems with Gen2 ingestion. Also during this time, Gen3 will track the file in a posix datastore along with Rucio tracking the file for replications. An assumption is that the raw image should be moved into the final storage location before ingesting into Rucio or any butler repository. These mean that all ingestions (Rucio, Gen2, and Gen3) should be independent. This epic should not be dependent upon whether Rucio or Gen3 ingestion is ready for deployment. This epic should assume that python code will be provided that:    * Will take a filename (including path) to ingest  * Will take a dictionary of configuration value(s) (may end up including name of other config file)  * Will throw an exception on error (Actual interface to be determined by design and prototyping)    This ticket had been created automatically  Primavera ID: A7830

title: Investigate Faust for the kafka-aggregator app
description: As proposed in DMTN-082 the LSP users are generally interested in telemetry data at a frequency closer to the cadence of the observations.     The original proposal is that “all telemetry topics sampled with a frequency higher than 1Hz are (1) downsampled at 1Hz and (2) aggregated to 1Hz using general statistics like min, max, mean, median stdev”.     Commands and event topics should not be aggregated as they are typically low-frequency and can be read directly from the raw EFD data sources.    Another aspect of the aggregation is to resample the telemetry topics in a regular time grid to make it easier to correlate them.    The aggregator will produce a new set of aggregated telemetry topics in Kafka that can be consumed by a connector and stored in a specific format. In another ticket we'll use the parquet data format to store the aggregated topics.     In this ticket, we'll investigate and evaluate [Faust|https://faust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/], a Python asyncio stream processing library. Faust supports Avro serialization and multiple instances of a Faust worker can be started independently to distribute stream processing across nodes or CPU cores.

title: Prototype datastore changes to support dataset disassembly/assembly
description: After some discussion we have decided that it might be better for datastore to be in charge of assembly/disassembly of datasets. Currently registry creates 7 rows per raw with almost none of those components being relevant. We did it this way to allow pipelines to specify components directly. We very rarely want to do this though and it would be more efficient in database storage to have a single row for a dataset in registry and move [dis]assembly to the datastore layer. Then we can instead write a single row if we do not disassemble and multiple rows if we do disassemble (and no row at all for components that were not present).  This is similar to the original implementation of datastore.    This ticket is to check that the approach is feasible and also whether it can be implemented independently of registry to allow us to experiment with both approaches in parallel.

This boils down to to making the necessary changes such that the following list of commands execute correctly, given the stated conditions, irregardless of whether the commands can be executed via a scons flag or not:    If provided a correct butler.yaml, AWS credentials, a S3 Bucket as repo root and an connectable RDS instance  {code:bash}makeButlerRepo.py --override s3://bucketname/ -c butler.yaml  registerInstrument.py s3://bucketname/  makeGen3Skymap.py s3://bucketname/ -C ~/ci_hsc_gen3/configs/skymap.py skymaps  ingestExternalData.py s3://bucketname/ ci_hsc_gen3/resources/external.yaml  pipetask run -d """"patch = 69"""" -b s3://bucketname/       -i calib/hsc,raw/hsc,masks/hsc,ref_cats,skymaps,shared/ci_hsc       -o shared/ci_hsc_output       --register-dataset-types       -p ci_hsc_gen3/pipelines/CiHsc.yaml    This stopped being the case when S3Datastore was implemented.  h2. *2. Improvements*  h3. *a. ingestExternalData.py script in ci_hsc_gen3 hard-codes """"symlink"""" transfer type*    Which is fine in context of **ci_hsc_gen3  scons but makes no sense in non-POSIX compliant cases. Add a flag to [ingestExternalData.py|https://github.com/lsst/ci_hsc_gen3/blob/master/bin.src/ingestExternalData.py#L41] that defaults to symlink but allows other transfer types to be specified.  h3. *b. makeButlerRepo.py creates a """"."""" key when a fresh S3 Bucket is targeted*    Does not break functionality but shouldn't happen. The """"."""" alias for absolute path shouldn't appear as a Key in the data repository root. Investigate and fix.  h2. *3. Extra goals*   * get a scons flag that wraps all the above instead of an external script or individual commands   * Add a way to turn checksums off. Talking to [~<USER> brought to my attention that this flag does not seem to be added to butler.yaml when DAF_BUTLER_CONFIG_PATH is set, but does if -c is explicitly provided. I suspect --override is missing/not applied in one case but is in the other. In any case if I want to get scons -aws (point directly above) then I'll have to mess with the SConfigure anyhow so I might as well investigate.   * See if timings for individual steps can be added as a flag to scons. Potentially useful but not reported by current scons is the timing breakdown of individual commands.

title: Avoid hammering login in Gafaelfawr
description: JavaScript sites will generate multiple login redirects that will not succeed, which can cause excessive upstream requests. It can also break CSRF handling by replacing the CSRF token in the session before the actual login attempt succeeds.    Fix both of these by reusing a state attribute if it hasn't expired and rate-limiting login redirects. (Or possibly detect JavaScript calls and don't redirect those?)

title: Add support for the MySQL-based empty chunk lists when ingesting new catalogs into Qserv
description: The current implementation of the Ingest System only supports the file-based *{{empty chunks lists}}*. Each catalog has a dedicated file. The files are located on a file system which is required to be seen (in the *{{read-only}}* mode) by each master node of a Qserv setup. This could be either a local or a network-based (NFS, GPFS, etc.) filesystem. In order to manage (populate, update, remove) the list the *{{Master Replication Controller}}* (providing the metadata services for the Qserv Catalogs Ingest workflows) is required to be run on a node which has the {{read-write}} access to a folder where the list are located. Depending on a setup of Qserv, it could be the same node where Qserv {{czar}} is setup, or be some other node which has a direct access to the folder. The current approach is have the empty file lists be deployed locally on each Qserv master node. The other issue is related to the multi-master extension of Qserv which is soon going to be deployed in production ({{lsp-int}}, {{lsp-prod}}) at {{NCSA}}. In such setup two (or as many as many Qserv master were configured - one per each Qserv {{czar}}) copies of the empty chunk list would have to be managed. The above explained ingest-lists """"affinity"""" requirement also complicates (makes it less flexible) the {{Kubernetes}}-based deployment scenarios for Qserv and its Replication/Ingest system. At the mean time the most recent versions of Qserv already support the lists as MySQL tables accessible by Qserv {{czar}} services. Potentially this allows to decouple a location of the lists from the hosts where Qserv `czar` and Replication/Ingest controllers run.    Hence a goal of this development is to add support for the empty chunk lists as MySQL tables. The REST API of the Ingest service needs to be extended with an option for choosing a desired persistent representation (a file system or a table) for the lists. The default value of the option should be the MySQL table. This could be changed if needed by passing an optional parameter to the service via the REST API.    The API extension will affect the following services:  ||method||service||role||  |{{POST}}|{{/ingest/chunk/empty}}|create or update an empty chunk list|  |{{PUT}}|{{/ingest/database/:name}}|publish a catalog (which also includes creating an empty chunk list)|

title: Measure Local-Sky Oversubtraction in HSC PDR1/PDR2/Current Data
description: In this notebook we have used statistics generated from sky objects to quantify and qualify sky over-subtraction and under-subtraction within Tract 9697. We performed three custom runs of coaddDriver to re-create HSC-SSP equivalent PDR1, PDR2 and PDR3 data using the current DM stack software. We further performed three custom runs of multiBandDriver using these data, extracting unmasked circular aperture fluxes within radii of 9 pixels and 250 pixels. Sky objects are pseudo-objects placed in regions where no other detections were found, and therefore should act as a measure of sky estimation success or failure across our dataset. Much of the analysis performed here leads on directly from efforts described in DM-23641.    We find significant variations in the sky estimation outputs employed over the course of HSC-SSP processing. PDR1 and PDR3 data visually exhibit significant sky-oversubtraction around bright sources, or in the vicinity of clusters of bright sources. These are likely caused by source flux or 'flux bridges' between bright sources being inadequetly identified at the source detection step, and included in a subsequent definition of a background sky map. Sky oversubtraction surrounding bright sources in PDR1 data gave rise to the term 'divot': the negative halo of flux surrounding bright sources. The radial extent of the divot in PDR1 lies further away from any given bright source than the equivalent divots in PDR3 data.    In PDR2 data, the divot issue appears largely to have been resolved, with minimal evidence for sky oversubtraction around bright sources. However, PDR2 data exhibits a much larger variation in background sky flux in the field, evidenced by sky oversubtraction in the least densely populated areas within this tract. The cause of this remains unclear, yet is likely linked to CCD and imaging artefacts (e.g., ghosts, ghoulies) compromising sky estimation efforts.    In summary, we find that all three datasets exhibit evidence of sky over-subtraction, either in densely populated regions (PDR3), sparsely populated regions (PDR2), or both (PDR1). The varying sky estimation routines employed here and their impact upon these performance metrics should be carefully considered when generating further improvements to our sky estimation routines in the future.    The attached notebook {{skycomp.ipynb}} contains all analysis and code. A PDF version of this notebook ({{skycomp.pdf}}) is also provided. The {{scripts.tar.gz}} file contains stack processing scripts and associated configuration files. All patch postage stamps may be viewed at this link: https://lsst-web.ncsa.illinois.edu/~<USER>skycomp/plots/0009697/

title: Investigate Faust windowing feature for data aggregation
description: In this ticket we implement an example to demonstrate the Faust [windowing|https://faust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userguide/tables.html] feature that can be used for aggregation of kafka streams.    The general idea is that you can use a Faust agent to process the stream of events  (messages) from a given Kafka topic and add those messages to a Faust table for persistence. The table is configured as a tumbling window. The window configuration parameters are a size and an expiration time. When the window expires a callback function is called to process the messages in that window. That's when the aggregation happens and a new Kafka topic is produced with the aggregated values.    A docker compose config is provided to start a local Kafka cluster to run the example. The instructions to start the Kafka cluster, the Faust worker and the producer are described in the README.  The docker compose also includes the Confluent Control Center which is handy to inspect the topics, their configurations and the consumer lag for the Faust consumers when running the application.    NOTE: running multiple Faust workers to distribute the application load currently crashes the application, this will be investigated in DM-24473.

title: Add abstractions for spatial indexing to daf.butler.registry.Database
description: Our current approach to spatial indexing on the sphere is simply to store the HTM IDs each region overlaps at a particular level, in an extra """"common skypix overlap"""" table for every table that has a region column.  This might be an okay approach for regions of a certain size, but it's definitely not a good approach for regions of arbitrary size, and probably not close to the best approach even for its ideal region size.  Doing better would probably require using special index types built for spatial overlap queries (R trees and variants thereof).  While the databases of interest to us (SQLite, Oracle, and PostgreSQL) do not support indexing regions on the sphere natively, they all do provide ways to index 3-d bounding boxes, and the lsst.sphgeom objects we work with provide ways to get 3-d bounding boxes (for a unit sphere).  The interfaces for the three databases are quite different, however, so the big challenge is probably encapsulating that functionality behind a consistent interface for the rest of our Registry code to use.  We might be able to leverage SQLAlchemy hooks for some of this customization, but I doubt they will cover everything.  While Oracle and PostgreSQL both treat geometries as column types and spatial indexes much like normal indexes, they have different syntax for inserting, querying, and relating them.  SQLite is even more different: its R tree implementation involves creating a special table for every spatial column, in which lower and upper bounds behave like regular (but separate) columms.  Adding at least some of the abstraction to our Database class might be a lot easier, and no less usable, though at present it doesn't do much with SELECT queries (they're just passed through to SQLAlchemy directly).  And I don't think this functionality needs to be totally transparent - just database-generic.  It would be totally reasonable for Registry code that's using our Database interface to work with a spatial column to have to do things it wouldn't have to do with a normal column, like manually extracting bounding boxes from regions for inserts, calling Database methods to get SQLAlchemy expressions that represent overlaps in query join/where clauses, or doing post-query filtering in Python (as we do now).  This ticket is for adding that abstraction layer to some combination of SQLAlchemy and the Database class.  I'll create another one for actually using it in Registry (maybe after the design for this one is further along).

title: Implement direct gradients in scarlet
description: Currently scarlet uses autograd to calculated the gradients used for optimization. This creates an overhead in both memory and runtime, as autograd requires a wrapper for all functions used in the code in order to back-propagate the gradients for each variable.    For scarlet we can calculate almost all of those gradients ourselves, eliminating the need to use autograd. The attached notebook demonstrates how this can be done, giving an outline of the runtime differences between autograd and direct gradients using a simplified modeling algorithm with a single back-propagation. It also demonstrates that gradients can be back-propagated up to 10 times faster per iteration when using gradients that we calculate ourselves, where the exact saving is based on the ratio of the PSF to the full size image (which translates into how much time we are spending on gradient calculation vs convolutions).    DM-23788 implements convolutions in real space, resulting in a model that allows us to calculate all of the gradients directly ourselves. However, it also demonstrates that real space convolutions are slower than those performed in k-space, so we are likely to use fft convolutions in production. We could in principle still use autograd to calculate the FFT convolution gradients for us, however since we only need the gradients for that single operation it will likely be easier to just implement a direct gradient for the FFTs as well (which may be as simple as calling a function in autograd).

title: Handling mismatches in collections of chunks when ingesting director and dependent tables into Qserv
description: h1. Objectives    Both fixes were triggered by: https://jira.lsstcorp.org/browse/DM-24396    h2. Missing chunk contributions    In Qserv all partitioned tables of the same catalog (database) are expected to have _exactly_ the same set of _chunks_. The current implementation of the Replication/Ingest system _generally_ supports this requirement. This is enforced at the final stage of the ingest workflows - when _publishing_ catalogs. Unfortunately, this measure is not sufficient to sanitize user input at earlier stages where the problem could be properly addressed and missing chunks could be easily (and correctly) compensated by the *Ingest* system.  h3. Solution #1  From a technical point, a solution would be to create _chunk_ tables for all _partitioned_ tables each time a new contribution is received by the system for _any_ partitioned table. In this model any chunk touched by a user will result in a full set of all _partitioned_ tables created for that chunk, regardless if some chunks for some tables will be still empty after publishing a catalog.  h3. Solution #2  Unfortunately, the proposed solution only works if a collection of chunks for the subsequently loaded tables is a superset of the ones from the previous loading stages. Otherwise, chunks in the non-empty intersect would still be missing in Qserv. Hence the second solution implemented in the ticket was to add a _fix up_ stage run by the database _publishing_ algorithm to create missing tables. This would ensure all missing chunks of all relevant tables would be created.  h2. Fixing a bug in the {{CSS}} configurations of the _dependent_ tables  As it was reported in https://jira.lsstcorp.org/browse/DM-24396 Qserv fails to process queries involving dependent tables. The problem has been found in an an implementation of an algorithm populating the Qserv's {{CSS}} for the _dependent_ tables.   h2. Other minor fixes and improvements  * reinforced transaction management not to leave """"dead"""" (unnoticed by user's workflow) transaction in case if any problems occurs  during transaction creation  * reinforcing database publishing service to prevent the operation if it's too early to do so  *

title: Probable race in ci_hsc_gen3 SConstruct
description: On DM-15536, I discovered that the {{pipeline}} target in the ci_hsc_gen3 SConstruct file only depends on the {{raws}} target (and since that ticket, the {{visits}} target), but it should depend on the {{externals}} target as well.  I think this leaves correct execution up to whether SCons happens to schedule things in the right order.  I tried a few (failed) approaches to fixing this quickly that I'll document here:  - Just adding the dependency creates a cycle (or so SCons thinks), because some of the external files get dropped into the output collection/directory (!).  - Not telling SCons about the external files that get put into the output directory prevents {{scons --clean}} from deleting them.  - Moving those files out of the output directory by changing their entries in the YAML file is no good, as that will cause this to break next time we run the script that recreates the YAML file from ci_hsc_gen2 outputs.  I think the right fix has to involve moving those files to a different location in ci_hsc_gen2 as well.

title: Investigate solutions to enabled Avro in a Faust application
description: There are at least two packages of interest in PyPI to enable Avro in Faust applications.    I first looked at the [python-schema-registry-client|https://github.com/marcosschroh/python-schema-registry-client] package which implements a synchronous Confluent Schema Registry client and a [codec for Faust|https://github.com/marcosschroh/python-schema-registry-client/blob/master/schema_registry/serializers/faust_serializer.py].    See more about Faust codecs and using different serializers in the [Faust documentation|https://faust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userguide/models.html#codecs].    The other package out there is [faust-avro|https://github.com/masterysystems/faust-avro] which also implements an Avro codec and Confluent Schema Registry support for Faust.    Looking at the code {{faust-avro}} seems more attractive for its hability to [parse a Faust record into an Avro schema |https://github.com/masterysystems/faust-avro/blob/master/faust_avro/parsers/faust.py] I think that's an important feature missing in the {{python-schema-registry-client}} which assumes the Avro schema is provided in addition to the Faust record (see [here|https://github.com/marcosschroh/python-schema-registry-client/blob/master/schema_registry/serializers/faust_serializer.py#L32]).    In addition, the {{faust-avro}} implementation is asyncio based. A drawback, however, is that it subclasses the Faust base classes like {{faust.app.App}}, {{faust.serializers.codec.Codec}}, {{faust.serializers.schemas.Schemas}}, {{faust.models.record.Record}}, {{faust.types.topic.Topic}}, etc but that also makes using it much easier as we show in this ticket.    Perhaps a hybrid solution would be to use only the parsers implemented in {{faust-avro}} and our own library {{kafkit}} that already implements an async schema registry client.    I think that implies rewriting [faust_avro/serializers.py|https://github.com/masterysystems/faust-avro/blob/master/faust_avro/serializers.py] using kafkit as a [codec for Faust|https://github.com/marcosschroh/python-schema-registry-client/blob/master/schema_registry/serializers/faust_serializer.py] similar to what [python-schema-registry-client|https://github.com/marcosschroh/python-schema-registry-client/blob/master/schema_registry/serializers/faust_serializer.py] does.  However, I don't know if that's possible without changing the {{faust-avro}} source code.

title: Create Faust Records dynamically from Avro schemas
description: In {{kafka-aggregator}}, Faust agents aggregate the data stream on tumbling windows of fixed size (see DM-24403). Faust Records describe the data structure for the aggregated topics and with {{faust-avro}} we can serialize that to Avro.    Generally, a field representing a value in the source topic will have the corresponding aggregation fields e.g. min, mean, median, and max in the destination topic.     In DM-24485 we demonstrated that we can parse a Faust Record into an Avro schema with {{faust-avro}} which allows us to register schemas for the aggregated topics in the Schema Registry.    However, we still need to create the Faust Record for the aggregated topic in the first place.    The goal for this ticket is to demonstrate we can create the Faust Record classes dynamically, otherwise, we would have to pre-generate a large amount of static code to create Faust Records for each schema we have in the EFD.

title: Assign the OFC state0 in ts_MTAOS by Configuration File
description: Assign the OFC (Optical Feedback Control) state0 in ts_MTAOS by configuration file. The *ConfigurableCsc* class in ts_salobj is the basic CSC (Commendable SAL Component) class for the subsystem such as *MtaosCsc* in ts_MTAOS to use. The configuration file is located at MTAOS directory of ts_config_mttcs. The following document explains the details of this: [TSTN-017|https://tstn-017.lsst.io/]. When writing the configuration file, a schema is needed to verify the configuration file based on: [Write a CSC|https://ts-salobj.lsst.io/salobj_cscs.html#writing-a-csc].    OFC is the component that calculates the correction of mirror bending mode and hexapod position. The control algorithm in use can follow [Real time wavefront control system for the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope (LSST)|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RyMQWeXWRZLtxM8KkSwtB3STzMM9fCvX/view?usp=sharing] and [Control Algorithm in Optical Feedback Control|https://confluence.lsstcorp.org/display/LTS/Control+Algorithm+in+Optical+Feedback+Control]. The state0 (*s*~*0*~ in the [Control Algorithm in Optical Feedback Control|https://confluence.lsstcorp.org/display/LTS/Control+Algorithm+in+Optical+Feedback+Control]) is an intentional parameter used in *x00* reference, which is explained in the above links.    The AOS software contains the simulation code and control code. For the simulation, the user needs to use the repos: ts_wep, ts_ofc, and ts_phosim. For the control code, the user needs to use the repos: ts_wep, ts_ofc, and ts_MTAOS. The ts_phosim is not needed in the control and the ts_MTAOS is not needed in the simulation. In this task, we focus on the control code.    The followings are the steps in this task:   # Update the [default.yaml|https://github.com/lsst-ts/ts_config_mttcs/blob/develop/MTAOS/v1/default.yaml] in ts_config_mttcs to contain the state0 information as the following: [state0inDof.yaml|https://github.com/lsst-ts/ts_ofc/blob/master/policy/comcam/state0inDof.yaml]. I prefer to have two yaml files (default.yaml + state0inDof.yaml) instead of one (default.yaml) in ts_config_mttcs. However, we need to check ts_salobj can support this or not.   # Provide the related schema: [MTAOS.yaml|https://github.com/lsst-ts/ts_MTAOS/blob/master/schema/MTAOS.yaml] in ts_MTAOS/schema directory. Prefer to have two files instead of one. But this depends on the implementation of ts_salobj.   # Update *MtaosCsc* class in ts_MTAOS to read the configuration of state0. *MtaosCsc.configure()* will read the configuration file from SAL. *ConfigByObj* and *ConfigByFile* classes inherit from *ConfigDefault* to read the data. We need to update the related test cases to make sure the *MtaosCsc* can change the state0 by SAL or file.   # Override the default state0 when *OFCCalculation* is instantiated by *OFCCalculationFactory.getCalculator()* in *Model.ofc*. The state0 is stored in the internal data of *Model.ofc.ztaac.optCtrl*. The developer can do *OFCCalculation.getZtaac()* to get the *ztaac* attribute. After this, the developer can use *ZTAAC.setState0()* to set the state0 values. The related *get()* functions are provided for the test. By default, the state0 is set by *OFCCalculation()* --> *OFCCalculation._configZTAAC()* --> *ZTAAC.setState0FromFile()*. It is noted that we will keep the default state0 file in ts_ofc for the simulation (the AOS simulation does not know the ts_MTAOS. The UW team is using the AOS simulation to help the algorithm development)   # Update the test cases and [versionHistory.rst|https://github.com/lsst-ts/ts_MTAOS/blob/master/doc/versionHistory.rst] to reflect the change.

title: Improve Gen3 schema backwards compatibility
description: The registry refactor to delegate to polymorphic helper classes should allow us to make many different kinds of changes to the Registry implementation that affect the database schema without breaking our ability to read old repos with new code.  Actually making that happen requires a number of smaller changes, and there are many more that would further improve our backwards compatibility situation:   * copying (and effectively freezing) the Registry config subtrees for dimensions and manager classes into per-repo configs, instead of always pulling defaults from daf_butler;   * starting to increment the version number in the dimensions config;   * recording the dimensions version in the database somewhere, so we can easily check for consistency and raise more helpful exceptions when the config is inconsistent with the database;   * recording the manager classes used in the database (for the same reason), and perhaps adding version numbers for these as well;   * adding dimension version numbers or some other form of stability to the byte-encoded form of DimensionGraph   * recording the names of dynamic tables in the static tables that manage them to reduce reliance on any particular name format   * making it so Manager classes that add foreign key fields can use compound keys, further encapsulating DDL schemas inside the managers.    Note that this ticket is about reducing the need for schema migration (or at least giving us more flexibility about when any particular repo is migrated).  We'll still need to have some way to do actual schema migrations to upgrade old repos when they can't just be thrown away.

title: Replace confluent_kafka with a python Kafka library that is more robust for alert-stream-simulator
description: The `confluent_kafka` library is currently used in alert-stream-simulator for producing to Kafka. It turns out that this library will never actually raise errors of any kind on connection problems. It can be given a timeout, but it will timeout silently with no message. title: Extend the Replication/Ingest framework and REST API with algorithms and tools for indexing catalogs
description: The current implementation of the Replication/Ingest doesn't provide any mechanism for managing (inspecting, creating or dropping) indexes on the data tables within Qserv. Only a few essential (for Qserv to function) indexes get automatically created. A lack of indexes may affect a performance of many user queries. Hence a goal of this development is to add the following capabilities to the system:  * extending the Replication Framework with a set of _request_ and _job_ classes for managing indexes at workers.  * adding a command-line version of the Replication _controller_ tool for managing the indexes  * extending the REST services of the *Master Replication Controller* with the index management services    Other notes:  * the REST services need to be protected with the _auth_key_ mechanism as explained in: https://jira.lsstcorp.org/browse/DM-22745  * it may be necessary to consider putting a cap on the number of indexes which were created by the system due to disk space constraints at a particular Qserv deployment. For example, the system may need to evaluate the amount of the available disk space on the coresponding file system (at Qserv workers) before attempting to create a new index.

Hence a goal of this development is to add the following capabilities to the system: * extending the Replication Framework with a set of _request_ and _job_ classes for managing indexes at workers. * adding a command-line version of the Replication _controller_ tool for managing the indexes * extending the REST services of the *Master Replication Controller* with the index management services Other notes: * the REST services need to be protected with the _auth_key_ mechanism as explained in: https://jira.lsstcorp.org/browse/DM-22745 * it may be necessary to consider putting a cap on the number of indexes which were created by the system due to disk space constraints at a particular Qserv deployment. For example, the system may need to evaluate the amount of the available disk space on the coresponding file system (at Qserv workers) before attempting to create a new index.

An interesting alternative for the control center is the [Lenses dashboards| https://docs.lenses.io/1.1/using-lenses/user-guide/dashboard.html]    We plan on investigating these alternatives in the next epic for the EFD.

title: Improved error reporting in the REST services of the Replication System's Master Controller
description: There are a few problems with the current design of the HTTP modules (subclasses of {{lsst::qserv::replica::HttpModule}}):  * it's impossible to return an extended description of errors in addition to a simple string sent back to the services' requestors. It would be useful for many operations to let a client have more insight into origins of problems reported by some services.  * the general design for reporting both results and errors is unsafe, and it leaves a room for mistakes.    In the current model a module's implementation has to use the following mechanism for reporting results/errors:  {code:c++}  class HttpSomeModule: public HttpModule {  ...  protected:      virtual void executeImpl() override {          ...          if (error condition) {              sendError(""""error string"""");              return;          }          ....          json result = ... ;          sendData(result);          return;      }      ....  };

title: Add accurate client IP addresses to Gafawlfawr logs
description: The client IPs shown in Gafaelfawr logs for the {{/auth}} endpoint currently point to the NGINX ingress pod instead of the actual client IP.    The problem is that the {{/auth}} request flow is route -> internal handler -> auth route. The internal handler passes the correct remote IP to the auth route, but because it adds another proxy step, the auth route itself sees the IP of the NGINX server as the request IP and sets a new {{X-Forwarded-For}} pointing to NGINX.    We need to reconfigure the ingress to not clear {{X-Forwarded-For}} and instead append to it, which in turn means that Gafaelfawr needs to know how far back to look in the {{X-Forwarded-For}} chain to know what the first external IP is (otherwise you end up trusting random {{X-Forwarded-For}} headers sent by a client, which isn't desirable).    That will affect everything, so all services behind that ingress will get the full {{X-Forwaded-For}} header. Hopefully that won't break anything else; anything that needs to trust that header will need to be configured with the deployment IP range so that it knows what the first external IP is.

title: Create dataset class for processed bright star stamps
description: As part of bright star wings/extended PSF model (DM-23785), we will extract stamps around bright stars from calexps, apply some preprocessing, then save these (along with some metadata) to disk.    The reason this is needed is the code for DM-23785 will rely on coadding a very large number of small cut-outs around bright stars, from different calexps, together. These require some preprocessing steps, such as a normalization step, before being coadded. Since we cannot possibly store all stamps in memory at once, we cannot do this processing on the fly before coaddition, hence the choice to save them to disk.    Longer term, this choice will also enable us to change the way we build the extended PSF (aka bright star wing) models without having to redo the processing. As an example, we might (and likely will) come to realize we want a different extended PSF model for each CCD, or at least per some subregion of the full focal plane. If our initial run had all stars stacked together to build a single, constant model, we could reuse the processed stars saved at this stage to build the new models.    Regarding normalization of the stamps: while this will be carried out in the code for DM-23785, it is worth mentioning here. Since very bright stars are saturated, and otherwise contain various ghosts around their center, we cannot use usual (say, aperture) measurements of their flux. What we will do is instead integrate their flux in an annulus of constant radii around their center, far out enough that most ghosts are contained within the inner radius and do not impact this """"annularFlux"""" measurement. These values (one per star/stamp) are one of the things stored in the dataset introduced by this ticket. These only make sense in relation to one another if the annulus definitions used are the same; the class therefore contains checks that the same annulus radii (both inner and outer) are used, every time new stamps are added to the collection.       This ticket will add the class itself, and the associated info in obs packages.

title: Register aggregated topic schemas to a secondary schema registry
description: In the EFD, data replication is done in one direction, copying kafka topics and schemas from a source cluster (e.g. base) to a destination cluster (e.g.  LDF) (see the multi Data Center [active-passive setup | https://docs.confluent.io/current/schema-registry/multidc.html])    The Aggregator is a component that runs on the destination cluster (e.g. LDF) and it creates new schemas for the aggregated topics.  In the active-passive setup, these schemas will exist only at the destination cluster, we don't want them replicated back to the source cluster. That means the schema IDs would no longer be globally unique if we use the same Schema Registry to register the aggregated topic schemas, there may be collisions between schema IDs for schemas created at the source and destination clusters.     For the Aggregator, we'll need *a secondary schema registry* to register the aggregated topic schemas.     In this ticket, we'll investigate this possibility further and configure the {{kafka-aggregator}} to read schemas for the source topics from the primary Schema Registry and write schemas to the secondary one.

title: salobj test failures involving SALPY that look like delayed late joiner data
description: [~<USER> is seeing fairly consistent unit tests failures in ts_salobj on the Tucson test stand: this is only in the tests of communication between SALPY-or-salobj and SALPY-or-salobj. I have appended the log of the most recent failure, which is between SALPY and SALPY.    The way the test works is:  * Runs a simple Test controller/server (in this case using SALPY) as a background job. This controller listens for setLogLevel commands and every time it receives one it echoes the commanded log level using two topics: the {{logLevel}} event and the int0 field of the {{scalars}} telemetry topics. If the commanded level is 0, the controller then waits one second and exits (but that detail does not appear to be relevant to the failures).  * It runs a Test remote/client (again in this case using SALPY) that talks to the controller.  * It reads and checks the initial value of the logLevel event (20)  * It commands several other log levels (the final value being 0). Each time it commands a new log level it waits for the new value to show up in the logLevel event and scalars telemetry.  * The test fails after sending and successfully checking a value or two (so at least one non-20 values has been read). The remote reads a value of 20 when it expects some other value that it just commanded.    This strongly suggests that SALPY is somehow duplicating the initial logLevel sample.    My first though was that {{wait_for_historical_data}} was timing out before the data arrived (the test stand is a bigger environment than my computer and Jenkins so it may take longer for that data to arrive). As you know, if the timeout is too short then late joiner samples will show up after new samples have arrived. I'm not sure if that's a general flaw with DDS or just a misfeature/bug in OpenSplice, but it's a serious problem.    So I asked Adam to set LSST_DDS_HISTORYSYNC=300. But the test still fails (in fact the failure log below had that value of env variable set). So unless SALPY is ignoring that environment variable or the test is taking longer than 300 seconds to run, I think we can rule out that explanation.    Adam sees it almost every time on the Tucson test stand, so that seems like a good place to explore it. I also see it as an intermittent error in the Jenkins job (and I think more often than with SAL 4.0). I never see it on my Mac.

title: Remember which dataset types are in various collections
description: We may be able to optimize dataset lookups by remembering which dataset types are present in various collections.    This could happen down in daf_butler, for every collection, via some kind of materialized summary view of the dataset_collection_ tables (which could be managed either by Python code or by database support for materialized joins).  It could also happen by using CHAINED collections more as the """"user visible"""" collections created by the ingest and conversion scripts, because CHAINED collections already permit the dataset types looked up in child collection to be restricted.  The former is more work but seems cleaner long-term (there may be some potential for surprising behavior if we rely only on the latter), and we may want to do the latter as well anyway.    This would probably require schema changes, but probably only additions, and it may be doable in a way that allows the old schema and new schema to both be supported via configuration changes.

title: Modifying published catalogs and tables in Qserv
description: The present implementation of the Replication/Ingest system's management system already supports deleting partially ingested catalogs (not tables) using the following resource:  ||method||resource||  |DELETE|/ingest/database/:name|    Unfortunately, the present mechanism leaves behind a number of other use cases which are still important. Hence the *main* objective of the proposed effort is to extend the existing implementation of the system's management interface (the REST API) to allow deleting select tables from the *non*-{{published}} catalogs as well as tables from the {{published}} catalogs, or the whole catalogs. These are examples of catalogs which may need to be deleted:   * test catalogs   * obsolete or wrong (based on the incorrect input) catalogs   * catalogs for which a new (better) version had been ingested   * less important catalogs (to clear disk space in Qserv workers before ingesting more important ones)   * catalogs contributed by users if a users is n longer interested in the catalog    The *second* objective of the effort is to implement a mechanism for *un-{{publishing}}* catalogs. In addition to the above stated scenarios, this one would also allow _extending_ existing catalogs with more tables, _chunks_, adding rows to existing _regular_ or _partitioned_ (_chunked_) tables, removing rows (based on a specific {{super-transaction}}) from existing _regular_ or _partitioned_ (_chunked_) tables. The proposed _bi-directional_ transitions of catalogs between the {{published}} and *non-*{{published}} states would be needed for   * QA-ing large catalogs during their _incremental_ ingests   * fixing problems with catalog ingests which were discovered during QA. This would be done by removing contributions into the catalog made during a specific {{super-transaction}}   * supporting user-level (contributed) catalogs which may be less static by their very nature compared with the production ones (LSST DRP, etc.)    Additional requirements/restrictions:   * all operations affecting *non-*{{published}} catalogs should begin with *un-*{{publishing}} a catalog first.   * the operations affecting the {{published}} catalogs will require adding extra security (management privileges) on top of what was already implemented with the {{auth_key}} based authorization: https://jira.lsstcorp.org/browse/DM-22745. One option here which won't require changing the protocol would be to discriminate different values of the keys to treat some of those as the """"high privilege"""" ones.   * the operation should *not* allow deleting the {{director}} table alone unless the whole database is being deleted.    Deleting a table requires eliminating the following data within Qserv and the Replication system's configuration:   * all instances of the table at workers   * an instance of the table from the {{information_schema}} table at Qserv {{czar}}'s database   * the the corresponding entry from {{CSS}}   * the table entry from the Replication System's Configuration    Deleting a whole catalog (database) requires deleting:   * all instances of the database at workers   * an instance of the database from the {{information_schema}} table at Qserv {{czar}}'s database   * the the corresponding entry from {{CSS}}   * the {{secondary_index}} for the {{director}} table of the database   * the {{empty chunk list}} file or the table.   * the database entry from the Replication System's Configuration    The proposed operation of *un*-{{publishing}} a catalog requires:   * eliminating the catalog from {{CSS}} to prevent Qserv from seeing the catalog   * reinstalling MySQL partitions (or creating the default partition *0* if none existed before) at all tables of the catalog. This step should also affect the {{secondary index}}    The the following resource are to be added:  ||method||resource||role||  |DELETE|/ingest/table/:name|deleting select tables of the *non*-{{published}} catalogs|  |PUT|/replication/database/:name|*un*-{{publish}} a catalog, so that it could be further modified|

title: Rework testdata_jointcal dependencies
description: The new data in DM-17597 will grow the size of a testdata_jointcal checkout significantly. Because testdata_jointcal has dependencies on each of the obs packages that it contains data for, it is re-installed during every build, resulting in potentially significant disk usage.    This ticket is to split out the obs dependencies so that testdata_jointcal has no dependencies itself. jointcal and fgcmcal would then gain optional dependencies on the obs packages whose repos they use, in addition to testdata_jointcal. Those unittests would also need to trip for whether the appropriate obs packages was `setup` and skip the tests if not.    As part of this, we should add a note to `fgcmcal.table` to explain why it has a dependency on jointcal (it needs the gen2 tract-grouping code, which will be unnecessary in gen3).

title: Unclear error messages in pipetask run
description: While trying to figure out {{pipetask run}} and a new pipeline simultaneously, I've encountered the following error messages that I believe could be improved:  * If I omit the {{--butler-config}} argument, I get {{sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: collection}}. It would be more helpful to warn that no Butler repository has been found/selected.  * If I have a mismatch between the dimensions  of a dataset as listed in PipelineTask connections and in the registry, I get {{ValueError: Supplied dataset type \[dataset] inconsistent with registry definition \[dataset]}}. It would help to also mention which task is the problem; the stack trace is all from general-purpose code.  * If I can't account for a particular dataset, I get {{RuntimeError: Expected exactly one instance of input \[dataset]}}. As above, it would help for debugging to know which task is being processed.  * If I omit the {{--register-dataset-types}} argument, I get {{KeyError: """"DatasetType \[dataset] could not be found.""""}}, suggesting that there is a matching problem with the pipeline. Given that this is an extremely common user error, it would be helpful to suggest that it might be a registration problem instead.  * If I forget to provide an {{--input}} when it's mandatory, I get an {{Expected exactly one instance of input}} error with a seemingly arbitrary data ID. This message misleadingly suggests the problem is with the dataset, not the collection.  * An invalid storage class raises a bare {{KeyError}}. It would be more helpful to report which connection and/or which dataset type caused the error.  * If I pass a {{--data-query}} argument that does not match any IDs, I get {{UnboundLocalError: local variable 'n' referenced before assignment}}. An empty query should be handled explicitly by the code.  * If I'm running on a repository with an out-of-date schema, I get {{sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) attempt to write a readonly database}}. title: Fix non-normalized matching kernel case in the decorrelation afterburner
description: In DM-24371, the implemented afterburner correction implicitly assumes that the _matching kernel_ is sum == 1 which is not usually the case, especially without scaling the science and reference image values by their photometric calibration.   * The afterburner correction does not sum to 1, which changes the fluxes of the difference image (or shift its photometric scale).   * The variance plane calculation of the afterburned difference image is scaled to the level of var1+var2 which is incorrect if the matching kernel contains flux rescaling, i.e. not sum == 1.   * The same consideration is required to support a _preconvolution_ kernel, though it needs further investigation to determine the statistical meaning of an _afterburned_ _preconvolved_ image.   * Also, this causes the corrected PSF not to be automatically sum == 1, though this is corrected by the {{KernelPsf}} creation.

title: Implement proper variance plane calculation in the decorrelation afterburner
description: In the DM-24371 implementation, we throw away the difference image variance plane as it cannot be afterburned due to unaccounted covariances. However the variance plane calculation from the originals does not consider the effect of the overall (afterburned) convolution of (the original) pixels at the moment which it could do.    For more accurate variance plane calculation, re-do the variance plane operations separately on the science and template image original variance planes using the idea of ZOGY eq. (26)-(27) then add them. This is expected to increase the CPU cost by x4 of the afterburner. Consider keeping this approach optional, especially not doing on the spatially varying case just once for the whole image.

title: Make it clear that gen3 instrument class paths don't need .instrument
description: In DM-23980 I standardized the instrument class names for Gen3. Doing so means that both {{lsst.obs.lsst.LsstCam}} and {{lsst.obs.lsst.instrument.LsstCam}} work. Since we don't want multiple ways of specifying the same instrument and we already know of cases where people think they need to include the {{.instrument}}, rename the internal {{instrument.py}} to {{_instrument.py}} to make it clearer that this name should not be used. title: Gen 2->3 conversion of DECam repositories can give duplicate defects
description: If I convert a DECam Gen 2 repository containing defects, the conversion succeeds, but running {{ProcessCcd}} on the result gives an error:    The immediate cause is that one copy of the defects is from the Gen 2 repository, the other copy was ingested during the conversion.    Discussion on [#dm-middleware|https://lsstc.slack.com/archives/C2JPT1KB7/p1590719387081900] suggests that this is due to conflicting responsibilities:  * {{obs.base.Instrument}} has some [hard-coded definitions|https://github.com/lsst/obs_base/blob/a51665517dd0ecacd8d72fbcead186475fcf66d3/python/lsst/obs/base/instrument.py#L38-L45] of curated files, which are processed any time {{ConvertRepoConfig.doWriteCuratedCalibrations}} is set. Defects are included.  * {{ConvertRepoConfig}} also has a [{{curatedCalibrations}} field|https://github.com/lsst/obs_base/blob/7c071951e367c4bef83840b75921f3a2f3af29cb/python/lsst/obs/base/gen2to3/convertRepo.py#L252-L263], which presumably allows other datasets to be handled using {{writeCuratedCalibrations}}. This list does not include defects by default.  * HSC [adds defects to {{ConvertRepoConfig.curatedCalibrations}}|https://github.com/lsst/obs_subaru/blob/c641360ad764cf8db63ecf1d14af6c93660160ff/config/hsc/convertRepo.py#L35-L36]. The bug described above *does not* occur.  * DECam makes no changes to {{curatedCalibrations}}, and its [config override file|https://github.com/lsst/obs_decam/blob/8567ae41add358da7b9af65fc81c39e39078b975/config/convertRepo.py] makes no mention of defects. The bug *does* occur.    The above behavior implies that DECam repositories with defects cannot be converted using the default configs, which goes against our general aim to provide working defaults for all Tasks.    Possible solutions:  * Do away with {{ConvertRepoConfig.curatedCalibrations}}, as proposed by [~<USER>. However, this does raise the question of how to handle observatory-specific curated calibrations.  * Have DECam explicitly register defects in {{curatedCalibrations}}, as HSC does. May be hard to scale to other instruments.  * Duplicate the dataset types hardcoded into {{Instrument}} in the default {{ConvertRepoConfig.curatedCalibrations}}. Won't benefit configs that overwrite this field instead of appending to it.

title: Have jointcal fail if the chi2 increases dramatically between steps
description: [~<USER> reported a [jointcal failure|https://lsstc.slack.com/archives/C2JPXB4HG/p1590742434125100] where the fitter went from {{chi2/ndof~=40}} to {{~1e7}} during a single rejection step. That suggests something went catastrophically wrong with the fitter at that stage. I think the fit loop should probably exit in this case, with an appropriate error message, and not try to write output files. A related question is what to do when the fitter does not converge after {{max_steps}}: currently jointcal logs an error but continues to attempt to write output. We should probably include a test for the chi2 value at the end of {{_iterate_fit}}, like was added in DM-15241 for a """"converged fit"""".

title: Redeploy Kafka on the NCSA test stand and investigations after the cluster intervention
description: On May 28th there was maintenance on the NCSA test stand cluster to replace weave CNI plugin by flannel.    I have restarted the EFD services on May 28th and it seemed to be working for some CSCs.    After starting all the CSCs we saw errors like:        That means the schema for a given topic was not registered when the producer started, or that it was registered with a different schema ID than the one used in the serialized message for that topic.    As a conseguence the connector tasks could not start properly and failed with the error above.    It looks like Kafka and the Schema Registry got to an inconsistent state and I suspect that happened because of network instability (?) as the producers and the EFD were running during the intervention.    Anyway, to fix that we stoped the producers and manually deleted that topic from Kafka and the corresponding schema from the registry.        Then we saw the problem for another topic, and repetitively to other topics. I only got the EFD working again after a fresh start i.e. redeploying Kafka removing all the previous topics and schemas :(

title: Implement agent code generation
description: The general idea is that you can use a Faust agent to process messages from a given Kafka topic and add those messages to a Faust table for persistence. The table is configured as a tumbling window. The window configuration parameters are the window size and the expiration time. When the window expires a callback function is called to process the messages in that window. That's when the aggregation happens and when a new Kafka topic is produced with the aggregated values.    In a previous ticket DM-24600 we created Faust records dynamically which saved us from generating static code for the models in Faust.    After some investigation, we concluded that it would be difficult to create the agent's code at runtime.  We'll try the approach of generating the code for the agents from a template and use Faust auto-discover mechanism to import the corresponding modules.

title: Please clean up the Dome events.
description: The existing Dome {{inPosition}} event has several serious problems:  * It has no boolean flag indicating whether or not the specified device is in position. We need to know """"is in position"""" and """"is not in position"""".  * It has a {{deviceId}} attribute, which badly breaks salobj's ability to automatically output new events only when data has changed. The most recent output is likely to be for a different device! Thus we will get far too many of these events, even when nothing has changed.  * The {{devicePosition}} field is not not useful (especially if you implement DM-25333) and is inadequate for the azimuth (without an associated velocity and time).    I suggest:  * A different inPosition event for each device/axis, e.g.:  * azimuthInPosition(inPosition=True/False)  * elevationInPosition(inPosition=True/False)  * etc.    An alternative is to have one or several events with multiple fields, e.g.:  * inPosition(azimuth=True/False, elevation=True/False, ...)  but it only makes sense to combine data that you get in a single status call. Otherwise you imply information that you don't have!    The same basic problem applies to most other events, including {{motionEnabled}} and {{driveFault}}, {{overTemp}}, {{speedLimitReached}}, {{accelerationLimitReached}} (why do those last two even exist?).  * It would be much better to have a separate event for each device  * We need a flag or other simple way to tell """"this condition is present"""" and """"this condition is absent"""".    Other changes to consider:  * Remove the word {{Change}} from all events that have that suffix. """"Change"""" is redundant. The event is being output *because* the state changed.  * Combine {{lockingPinEngaged}} and {{lockingPinDisengaged}} as {{lockingPin}} with a boolean {{engaged}} flag.  * Combine {{brakeEngaged}} and {{brakeDisengaged}} as {{brake}} with a boolean {{engaged}} flag.  * Combine {{motionEnabled}} and {{driveFault}} into {{driveState}}, with an enum field for enabled/not enabled/fault and another field for the fault code (which is null if enabled/disabled).  * Rename {{interlockAlarm}} field {{interlockAlarmCode}} to {{code}} and look for similar redundancies in other topics. There are a lot of fields that seem needlessly verbose (why """"devicePosition"""" instead of """"position"""", etc.)

title: base fails to build standalone

It seems that the YAML constructor assumes that {{Packages}} full name is {{base.packages.Packages}} rather than {{lsst.base.packages.Packages}}.  This causes the {{isinstance}} test to fail. title: Extend registry schema to support metadata/configuration
description: For schema stability we need a place where we can store identifying information for schema itself and various configuration-related info as well. That will server as a sort of metadata for the rest of the schema and data in registry. To be usable from many releases it itself needs to be super-stable but we also should be be able to store all sorts of metadata in it, exact structure of that is not possible predict today. I think the most generic solution for that is a simple key-value store with arbitrary keys and values encoded as strings. All other structures can be mapped to key/value using reasonable rules, though some care is certainly needed to avoid name collision.

title: Fix multiple writes into H&S FIFO in LabView Modbus library
description: LabView Modbus module (lsst-ts/Common_FPGA_Modbus) contains in RX subVi SCTL blocks where multiple calls into a singe FIFO are possible on timeouts. Those usually don't occurs, as the calls are after failed writes etc. which aren't expected. Still if they do happen, undertermined behaviour will follow - most probably FPGA will crash and communication with the M1M3 will be lost.         A prominent example is below. Update H&S is called to increase counter of received data. If write to RxDataFIFO timeout, update H&S is called to set flag 0x20. If stop bit (0x0200, 10th bit received) isn't true 0x10 is indicated among flags.         !image-2020-06-13-19-06-59-053.png!    It's hard to tell whatever a crash isn't a better solution to those unexpected problems. Hovewer, it will be much better to make it a controlled crash than un-controlled crash cased as side effect of multiple FIFO writes inside a single SCTL.    I hit the issue before while adding another code, realizing that LabView doesn't check writes inside subVis. It will not compile G code with direct (not hidden in subVi) multiple writes into a single FIFO in a single SCTL. LabView doc is full of warnings to not put multiple writes inside a single SCTL - see e.g. [https://forums.ni.com/t5/LabVIEW/FPGA-module-FIFO-arbitration-in-single-cycle-timed-loop/td-p/170803?profile.language=en.] The fact is also clear from how SCTL: works inside FPGA.

The Simulink model uses the *LsstCmdSet* object to get the time, position, and velocity of tracking target. If the user issues the *stop* command before the finish of slew, the rotator stops without the update of *LsstCmdSet*. This means if the user issues the *trackStart* command, the rotator will transition to the *SlewingAndTracking* sub-state and try to track the unfinished target based on *LsstCmdSet*.    In the following figure, there are two targets: (1) position=1.2 deg, velocity=0.01 deg/sec, and (2) position=3.0 deg, velocity=-0.01 deg/sec. The final *track* command is at time=6.05 second. Issue the *stop* command at time=7 second and *trackStart* command at time=9 second. We can see the rotator tries to finish the second target after it is back to the *SlewingAndTracking* sub-state.   !trackStopBeforeSlewDone.png|thumbnail!    To solve this problem, we need to update the *LsstCmdSet* object to set the position to be the rotator's position or position command, and the velocity to be 0 after the stop completes (*Flags_stopComplete* ==1.0) as the following:   !trackWithStopAnd3rdTargetOfPosNowAndRewiteCmdPosAndVel.png|thumbnail!    There are four possible options to do this:   (1) Update the *LsstCmdSet* object in *ts_rotator_controller* once *Flags_stopComplete*==1.0.   (2) Let *ts_rotator* update the *LsstCmdSet* object by sending the new *track* command once *Flags_stopComplete*==1.0. However, we prefer to use the command acknowledgement to know the *stop* command is finished or not in a latter time.   (3) Add a *reset* command or something similar in *ts_rotator* and *ts_rotator_controller* to let the rotator controller updates the position and velocity of *LsstCmdSet*.   (4) Update the Simulink model to add a latch to determine when to use the new *track* command. This will add the complexity to the Simulink model because it is not designed in that way originally. It may not be easy to debug in a latter time. However, this will not affect the *ts_rotator* and *ts_rotator_controller* at all.    I do not prefer the option 1 because there will be multiple places to write the data into the global variable of *LsstCmdSet*. Originally, it is updated by *ts_rotator* only. Or more accurately, the *ts_rotator* issues the *track* command to update the *LsstCmdSet* in *commanding.c* in *ts_rotator_controller*. If the option 1 is chosen, I need to let the *actuator.c* to be able to update the *LsstCmdSet* object. Think more deeply, for the option 3, it is the same thing. The only benefit for option 3 is that the CSC user knows the *LsstCmdSet* is changed. But if the CSC user does not care about this, maybe the option 1, 2, or 4 is better. If we consider the coherence of code, maybe the option 1 or 4 is the best solution.

title: Insert Fake Sources Provided by the LSST:UK LSB Working Group
description: The Rubin Obs DM team are actively collaborating with the LSST:UK LSB working group to develop LSB sky subtraction and source fidelity metrics. This ticket injects several fake source catalogues produced by the LSST:UK LSB WG into the stack, and analyses their outputs.     Resources:   * [Insert Fakes LSST Community link|https://community.lsst.org/t/new-tasks-for-fake-source-insertion/3722]  * [Insert Fakes source code|https://github.com/lsst/pipe_tasks/blob/master/python/lsst/pipe/tasks/insertFakes.py]    A number of input catalogues were provided, namely: {{model_faceon.fits}}, {{model_edgeon.fits}}, {{model_icl.fits}} and {{model_fornax_tab.fits}}. On closer analysis, a number of issues were discovered with these data, necessitating some modifications. Specifically, the requested pointings did not fall within tract 9813, one of our RC2 contuinally processed regions (see the tract figure attached below). To allow us to use these input data, we repositioned each object to move it into the centre of tract 9813. In addition, RA/Dec values were translated into radians, the column {{sourceType}} was added indicating that these sources are {{galaxy}} type, and Sersic indices were clipped to the range 0.3 < n < 6.2.     The modified Fornax dataset was processed using {{insertFakes}}, and then processed with detection turned on using {{multiBandDriver}}. To produce a final output object table, we finished processing using {{writeObjectTable.py}}, {{transformObjectCatalog.py}} and {{consolidateObjectTable.py}}. A trimmed version of this object table is attached to this ticket below.     All working is shown in the attached Jupyter Notebook, available in {{.ipynb}} or {{.pdf}} format below. We also include two example images below showcasing the insertion of a typical Sersic source in all five bands: one prior to final sky subtraction ({{deepCoadd}}) and one after final sky subtraction ({{deepCoadd_calexp}}).     All outputs are available via the LSP in this directory: {{/home/<USER>fakes_lsstuk/outputs/fornaxmod}}

title: Support read-only components for butler get
description: Currently we define components for StorageClasses to be the components that a dataset can be disassembled into or reassembled from.  This is fine for things like masks and wcs but gen2 supports read-only components such as BBox that allow you to efficiently query information about a specific dataset without having to fetch the entire dataset.    Getting this to work is fairly straight forward if there is no disassembly. If we do disassemble then I need to think about how we forward the BBox request to the correct component.

This is fine for things like masks and wcs but gen2 supports read-only components such as BBox that allow you to efficiently query information about a specific dataset without having to fetch the entire dataset. Getting this to work is fairly straight forward if there is no disassembly. If we do disassemble then I need to think about how we forward the BBox request to the correct component.

title: Implement M2 LUT behavior in m2 simulator
description: During our integration meeting we discussed that it would be helpful to have more behaviors added to the M2 simulator ([https://github.com/lsst-ts/ts_m2).] The obvious thing would be to implement the LUT. That means, the simulator will read the LUTs, listen to the telescope position and simulate applying the LUTs values to the different axis. This will allow us to study how M2 will behave during slews and help us identify any missing feature.     There are some relevant examples here: [https://github.com/lsst-sitcom/M2_summit_2003]

title: REST API for building the secondary index in Qserv
description: In the current implementation of the new Ingest system the _secondary index_ of a database is normally populated in the end of the _super-transactions_. The algorithm harvests contributions from the corresponding MySQL _partitions_ of the director table's chunks and loads them into the index table at Qserv """"czar""""'s database . Depending on the amount of data ingested into that table during a transaction the index building operation may noticeably slow down the commit phase of the transaction. After gaining the first experience with using the new Ingest system it has become apparent that some workflows may benefit from having the _secondary index_ construction as an explicit stage deferred till a moment when all director table's contributions were loaded into Qserv.    Hence, a goal of the current development is to refine and extend the REST API of the Master Replication Controller to allow more options in building the index. Specifically, the following changes are proposed:  * add an optional parameter *build_secondary_index=<val>* to existing database creation service to indicate an intent to defer the index creation till the very last stage. The default value of the parameter will be 0 which would preserve the current behavior.  * extend the database information structure DatabaseInfo with the corresponding flag.  * modify the transaction commit service not to make contributions into the index if the deferred index construction for the database was requested.  * add a new POST service for constructing indexes as a separate operation to be performed before (or with extra controls) after publishing a database. The service should also allow an optional parameter to allow rebuilding the index from scratch.  * update the documentation on the Ingest System accordingly.  * evaluate if the version of the Ingest API needs to be incremented as well.

title: Add support for the secondary index in sph-partition
description: h1. 1. Objectives    A goal of this effort is to add support for the _secondary index_ when partitioning data of the _child_ (_dependent_) tables. Here is the extended partitioning """"protocol"""":   # the partitioning is done based on either *{{RA}}*/*{{DEC}}* of a table, or a precomputed map *{{id -> (chunk,sub-chunk)}}*   # the *{{RA}}*/*{{DEC}}* mode is triggered by a presence of the following config or command line parameter *{{part.pos=<ra_column_name>,<dec_column_name>}}*   # to trigger an alternative partitioning method one would have to eliminate *{{part.pos}}* from the configuration and provide *{{part.id=<fk-to-director-table>}}*, where the """"foreign"""" key specified in the last parameter would be is the name of the corresponding column in the child table.   #* the partitioning of a dependent table will fail if an object identifier won't be found in the map   # if both *{{part.pos}}* and *{{part.id}}* are present then the former takes precedence over the later   # the *{{id -> (chunk,sub-chunk)}}* map gets created gets created if both *{{part.pos}}* and *{{part.id}}* are present. The map is stored in a file named *{{index.txt}}* at the same output destination where other partitioning products (chunks, overlaps) are stored.   # the *{{id -> (chunk,sub-chunk)}}* map files produced by the partitioner will be the {{CSV}}-formatted files following an output _dialect_ specified in a collection of parameters *{{part.out_csv.}}**  #* if the file already exist it will be open in the append mode, so that new object entries will be added to the file.   # if only *{{part.id}}* is present (indirect partitioning) then parameter *{{part.id-url=file:<path>/chunk_object_index.txt}}* is required by the partitioner   ** the partitioning of a dependent table will fail if no valid map will be provided   # the overlap tables are generated ONLY in the *{{RA}}*/*{{DEC}}* partitioning mode AND if *{{part.overlap != 0}}*   # the *{{id -> (chunk,sub-chunk)}}* map would *NEVER* be generated for the entries put into the overlap tables   #* that won't be needed because the _child_ (_dependent_) tables do not have overlaps in Qserv.    Other improvements:  * add partitioning option *{{part.disable-chunks={0|1}}}* to disable writing output chunked products. This mode would be used in the _dry run_ mode for evaluating input files, or for generating the _secondary_ index files for object tables which have been partitioned/ingested.    h1. 2. Design considerations and Requirements    In the initial (simplest) file-based implementation, the index files will be the regular *{{CSV}}* text files. Each line of the files will have the following format (assuming the _comma_-separated output formatting):    Where:   * there will be exactly one entry for each object encountered in the _director_ table's data file(s)   * values in each row of the file will be separated by a separator specified in the corresponding configuration parameters    h2. 2.1 Other notes/requirements   * consider using abstract interfaces for fetching data from the output index.   * consider implementing plugins for the abstract interfaces. Each such plugin would be mapped to the corresponding implementation of the persistent (or service-based) secondary index (examples: file-based, MySQL-based, REST API-based, Redis-based, etc.)
